questions.q: Why does Git handle large binary files badly by design?
options: It can't diff them meaningfully, so every version is stored close to full size, permanently ballooning the repository
Git refuses to store any file over 10MB
Large files corrupt Git's internal database
Git automatically deletes large files after each commit
questions.explain: Git's delta-encoding model works for line-based text but not opaque binaries, so large files bloat every version stored in history.

questions.q: What does Git LFS actually store in Git's own history for a tracked file?
options: A small pointer file containing a version tag, a hash, and a size
The full file content, just compressed differently
Nothing at all — the file is removed from Git entirely
A link to a website with no verification
questions.explain: Git LFS substitutes a tiny pointer file for the real content — that pointer is the entire thing Git actually commits and diffs.

questions.q: Where does `git lfs track` write the patterns it's given?
options: .gitattributes
.gitignore
package.json
The commit message
questions.explain: git lfs track writes matching patterns into .gitattributes, so matching files are automatically handled as pointers going forward.

questions.q: According to this lesson, when is Git LFS the WRONG tool?
options: For regenerable output like dbt's target/ directory, where .gitignore is the correct choice instead
For a versioned reference dataset that changes occasionally
For a trained model checkpoint that's part of the project's history
Any time a file exceeds 1KB in size
questions.explain: Files that regenerate every run (like dbt's target/) shouldn't be tracked at all — .gitignore is correct there, not LFS.

questions.q: What does this lesson recommend for a genuinely massive file, like a 400GB raw extract?
options: Store it in an object store like S3, with a link or manifest in the repo — not in Git at all, LFS or otherwise
Force it into Git LFS regardless of size
Split it into thousands of small commits
Email it to teammates instead of using version control
questions.explain: At data-lake scale, a file belongs in an object store rather than in Git, even with LFS, per this lesson's guidance.
